ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, UK HMT sanctions list, and Panama’s UAF / national police watchlists. Enhanced due diligence is implemented for politically exposed persons, their immediate family members, and close associates using risk-tiered continuous monitoring and source-of-funds verification for low-risk social commerce e-commerce merchants processing TikTok Shop payouts and Wise B2B transfers.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá — Portal de Trámites en Línea (RPL) at www.registro-publico.gob.pa
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names may be registered in Latin script in any language, but the foundation charter must contain a Spanish-language translation of the corporate name. Trade names must include or be accompanied by the term 'Fundación' or the abbreviation 'FIP' when the entity is a Private Interest Foundation. Non-Latin script names must be transliterated into romanized equivalents; the Registry will reject names that are graphically or phonetically confusing in Spanish or duplicative of existing registered names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: An extension of the name reservation may be filed with the Certification Office of the Registro Público before expiry; one extension of 30 days is available upon payment of the statutory fee. If the requested name is rejected, the applicant may submit an administrative appeal ('Recurso de Apelación') before the General Directorate of the Registro Público within fifteen (15) working days of notification. A second-level appeal may be brought before the Third Chamber of the Supreme Court of Justice on grounds of illegality or error in application of registry rules. A new name clearance request may be filed concurrently to avoid incorporation delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the statutory registered office of a Panama Private Interest Foundation. The PIF must maintain its registered address at the licensed resident agent’s physical office located in Panama. Virtual offices, co-working mailboxes, and nomad service centers may be used only as supplementary correspondence addresses and commercial service mailboxes; they cannot replace the resident agent’s physical statutory seat.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified 15-25% annual probability for a standard low-risk social commerce merchant operating through TikTok Shop and Wise B2B rails; probability rises to 40% or more where there is any PEP exposure, sanctions-adjacent counterparty, or cash-intensive secondary activity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Panama Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 on Private Interest Foundations, as amended by Law No. 2 of 2011 and Law 30 of 2015, Title I, Articles 1-29; Public Registry of Panama Resolution No. 201-2793 of 2013
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Public Registry of Panama - Private Interest Foundations Section (Seccion de Fundaciones de Interes Privado, Registro Publico de Panama)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foundation Charter (Escritura de Constitucion / Acta de Fundacion)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Private Interest Foundation Law requires a minimum initial endowment of USD 10,000 (or equivalent in convertible currency) to be declared in the Foundation Charter. There is no escrow or immediate paid-in requirement as long as the founder signs a formal acknowledgment of asset assignment; the foundation's patrimony becomes a segregated fund under Law 25, Article 4.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL OF "[NAME OF FOUNDATION]" ("FOUNDATION") - PANAMA.

WHEREAS the Foundation was registered as a private interest foundation under Law 25 of 1995, and its Charter provides for the administration of its patrimony;

NOW, THEREFORE, THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL RESOLVES:

1. The initial endowment contributed by the founder is formally accepted and recorded in the Foundation's books.
2. The registered office is the address designated in the Charter, within Panama City, Republic of Panama, for legal notices.
3. The officers named in the Charter are hereby ratified: President, Secretary, and Treasurer, with the Protector appointed to supervise the council.
4. The President and Secretary are jointly authorized to open bank accounts, execute commercial contracts for online retail operations, and pay all formation fees.
5. Certified copies of this Resolution shall be filed with the Public Registry.

Adopted unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama - Names and Trademarks Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the name search application with at least three proposed corporate names, each containing the word 'Fundacion' or 'Foundation'. The Registry verifies that the requested name is not confusingly identical to an existing legal entity. Upon clearance, a Certificate of Name Availability is issued, valid for 30 days.
required_dossiers: Three proposed foundation names in order of preference
Copy of founder's valid passport or identity card
Registry payment receipt for name search fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity, the applicant may file a written reconsideration petition within 10 business days, proposing a materially distinct second-choice name or using a corporate suffix variation; no additional search fee is charged.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of Panama (or Panamanian Consulate for foreign signatures)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Foundation Charter in Spanish specifying the founder, the initial endowment asset schedule, the foundation's purpose, the Foundation Council composition, beneficiary rules, and the Panama address. The formal document must be signed before a Panama Notary Public; if signed abroad, the signature must be duly legalized or apostilled and subsequently recognized by the Panamanian Consulate.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of founder and council members
Notarized acceptance letters from Foundation Council members
Initial asset schedule and source of funds declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a notarial defect is detected, the charter is revised and re-executed at a new notarial ceremony. Where consular legalization is defective, the document may be resubmitted through the Apostille Convention process; the Registry accepts a corrected certified copy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Presentation and Registration at the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama - Private Interest Foundations Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Foundation Charter to the Private Interest Foundations Section within 10 business days of notarization. Pay the state inscription fee. Use the expedited registration window to obtain a registration decision within 5 business days. The Registry examines the deed for legal form and records the foundation in the Public Registry of Foundations.
required_dossiers: Official tax receipt of inscription fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues an 'reasoned query' (reparo), the applicant has 5 business days to file a corrective brief and amended deed. If the application is rejected, an appeal (recurso de apelacion) lies to the Director General of the Public Registry within 15 business days, with a further option of judicial annulment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Registered Copy and Juridical Personality Certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama - Certification and Certificate Desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After inscription, request a certified copy of the registered foundation deed and a Certificate of Registration evidencing juridical personality. The private interest foundation attains legal existence from the date of registry inscription. Verify the foundation's economic number assigned by the Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered certificate contains a typographical error, file a written correction request under Article 24 of the Registry Rules; identical as provided by the Registrar's office for amendment or sweeping rectification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Identification Number (RUC) Registration with the Tax Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Direccion General de Ingresos (DGI, Ministry of Economy and Finance of Panama)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply online via the SIA platform or DGI window for the foundation's RUC. Present the registered Charter, proof of resident agent and registered office. If e-commerce sales generate Panamanian territorial income, register for VAT (ITBMS) when turnover exceeds USD 50,000 per annum. Obtain the RUC certificate before opening a bank account.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of registered Foundation Charter
Proof of physical address (lease or letter of access)
Designation of representative and resident agent acceptance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI issues an anti-rejection query regarding the nature of income, submit a territorial-source revenue declaration and a notarized business plan showing that income is derived from online sales to consumers, with supporting platform agreements. The RUC application may be resubmitted online.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Operation Notice and Ancillary Physical Premises Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipality of Panama (Alcaldia de Panama) and, if applicable, Fire Department and Ministry of Health
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a Municipal Aviso de Operacion for the e-commerce retail activity. The filing is a registration/notice, not an industrial license. If a physical office, warehouse, or fulfillment center is operated, require a fire safety inspection by the Cuerpo de Bomberos and an occupational clearance by MINSA. Keep a copy posted at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Signed copy of the Municipality Aviso de Operacion form
Lease contract or notarized authorization for physical premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Municipality suspends the Aviso de Operacion application due to incomplete documentation, correct and submit the missing items to the Municipality's Licensing and Oversight Unit within 10 business days. If the fire clearance fails, schedule re-inspection after installing corrective fire-extinguishing and evacuation measures.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - the foundation conducts non-industrial digital retail via TikTok Shop. The only operational registration that may apply is the municipal Aviso de Operacion, not a specialized industrial license.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Aviso de Operacion (Business Operation Notice) under the Municipality of Panama's commercial operations ordinance

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of Panama (MiAMBIENTE) - Water, Air and Environmental Quality Directorate
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (no full EIA) for pure e-commerce retail with no physical manufacturing. If a storage/logistics facility of more than 500 m2 is established, a Category I Environmental Registration under Resolution No. 046-2014 of MiAMBIENTE is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge, combustion or VOC emission is generated in the base operation. For any operational warehouse adopted: comply with Executive Decree No. 10 of 2011 for effluents (BOD5 max 50 mg/L, COD max 150 mg/L, TSS max 35 mg/L monthly averages) and Executive Decree No. 40 of 2017 for ambient air quality (PM2.5 max 25 ug/m3; PM10 max 50 ug/m3). Waste handling must be bid to an authorized disposal operator holding a MiAMBIENTE permit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection and evacuation certification under the National Civil Protection System (SINAPROC) and the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panama; structural load inspection and occupancy certificate from the Municipality of Panama for premises used above the ground floor; occupational workplace clearance issued by the Ministry of Labor and Workforce Development (MITRADEL) and Ministry of Health (MINSA) covering electrical installations, signage, and sanitary conditions.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Panama; electronic portal: https://dgi.mef.gob.pa (Sistema E-Tax / SIFDGI).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must appoint a resident legal representative and register with the DGI using Form 301 (Solicitud de Registro Único de Contribuyente). The representative must submit certified constitutional documents, proof of foreign registration, passport copies, a notarized power of attorney, and evidence of a local address. Upon approval, the DGI issues an RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) with a 11-digit numeric code; non-resident entities engaged in taxable activities without a permanent establishment may require simplified registration for withholding and digital services obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No U.S.-style check-the-box election exists under Panamanian law. Hybrid entity treatment is governed by the Private Interest Foundation Law (Law 25 of 1995, as amended) and tax regulations treating foundations as autonomous patrimonies without shareholders. Under the territorial system, only Panamanian-source income is taxable; no formal election is required to maintain pass-through or entity-level character for domestic purposes, but foundations may elect to register as a taxpayer and may opt into the simplified SME tax regime if qualifying under the relevant income thresholds. Cross-border hybrid mismatch elections are not available domestically; taxpayers rely on the Tax Code and the OECD position adopted through Panama's inclusion in the inclusive framework for information exchange.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios, ITBMS)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: PAB 150,000 (Panamanian Balboa, equivalent to USD 150,000) of annual gross revenue from taxable transfers and services for mandatory VAT registration; reduced thresholds apply for certain onerous transfers and for small taxpayers electing the simplified regime. Non-resident digital commerce operators may require registration irrespective of the threshold when supplying services to Panamanian consumers through local facilitating agents.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama operates a phased electronic invoicing regime under Decree 53 of 2018 and DGI Resolution 201-1410. Taxpayers must issue electronic invoices ('factura electrónica') through DGI-authorized software using the XML format and submit invoice batches to the DGI in near-real-time according to the authorized transmitter scheme. The DGI assigns a digital stamp ('impresión fiscal') and validates the invoice before transmission to the buyer. Foreign sellers using platforms such as TikTok Shop must ensure that the platform or local payment agent issues e-invoices for Panamanian sales; API integration is required for direct DGI clearance and digital stamping.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and services are generally zero-rated for ITBMS purposes when title passes outside Panama or the service is effectively used outside Panama. Offshore services provided by a Panamanian entity to non-residents, including digital commerce support services, are zero-rated if the recipient is outside Panama and the benefit of the service occurs outside the customs territory. Zero-rating is also available for goods removed from the tax jurisdiction under a valid customs export declaration and for services rendered to qualifying free-zone users.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA / Declaración Única de Aduanas approved by Panama Customs)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill proving physical departure of goods
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement evidencing foreign exchange repatriation
Commercial invoice issued by the exporter with explicit zero-rated ITBMS line
Export contract or purchase order identifying the non-resident buyer
Proof of payment of Panama-generated logistics charges or terminal handling certificates
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI may audit the complete export file, including customs logs, shipping manifests, banking records, and digital platform payout statements. Failure to substantiate zero-rating triggers retroactive collection of 7% ITBMS plus surcharges, monthly-adjusted interest, and fines ranging from 10% to 50% of the tax omitted depending on the degree of willful misconduct. Fraudulent export zero-rating claims involving false customs declarations, simulated offshore recipients, or unrepatriated foreign exchange may be prosecuted as tax evasion under the Fiscal Penal Code, with monetary penalties up to double the evaded tax and possible cancellation of the RUC, journalistic publication of the sanction, and restriction of the entity's ability to import or export through Panama.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Republic of Panama has no central bank and no dedicated foreign-exchange administration. Banking supervision and licensing are exercised by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP), established under Banking Law No. 42 of 2001; AML/CFT supervision is vested in the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) under Law No. 23 of 2015; fiscal-agent and public-depository functions are performed by Banco Nacional de Panamá; fiscal policy is coordinated by the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas. Panama is effectively dollarized: the Balboa is a unit of account and coinage at 1:1 parity with the United States dollar under the 1904 Monetary Convention and the associated monetary statute, and the U.S. dollar circulates as full legal tender.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates a full dollarization regime with zero exchange-control legislation, meaning there are no limitations on capital-account or current-account convertibility, no requirement for central-bank approval to open or operate foreign-currency accounts, no prior license to repatriate profits, and no obligation to engage in government-brokered conversions. Any conversion between USD, CNY, EUR or other currencies is executed as a private market transaction through licensed banks and international dealers. Profit remittance from a Panamanian Private Interest Foundation is unrestricted at the FX level; the only applicable gate is taxation under the territorial income-tax principle, under which distributions sourced from foreign commercial activity are outside Panamanian tax incidence, whereas Panamanian-source net profits attract the standard corporate and dividend withholding rules. The practical barriers to convertibility are not regulatory but documentary: banks require complete source-of-funds declarations, commercial evidence of the underlying TikTok Shop settlement flows, and CRS/FATCA self-certifications.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation timeline. A Panamanian PIF engaged in cross-border social commerce may retain 100% of TikTok Shop settlement proceeds in USD or any other currency in Panama or abroad, may hold them indefinitely, and may redeploy them to suppliers and beneficiaries without exchange-control authorizations. The only compliance conditions are general: every foreign receipt must be traceable to the platform settlement ledger and underlying invoices for income-tax territorial filing, and the bank's transaction-monitoring profile must reflect the declared e-commerce business volume to avoid money-laundering mischaracterization.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational clearing account and State fiscal-agent services
USD current account for TikTok Shop settlements and USD concentration account
Capital escrow account and private-banking custody for the Foundation's surplus liquidity
Trade disbursement account plus commercial letter-of-credit facility
USD operational current account with digital treasury platform
Merchant settlement account for card and e-commerce acquiring flows
USD operational account plus trade-finance guarantees
USD operational account and short-term deposits

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: HIGH for operational settlement facilitation, MEDIUM for the treasury core, LOW for long-term capital custody. Wise Business (TransferWise), Airwallex, Payoneer and similar foreign EMIs do accept Panama-registered entities and PIFs, provide USD collection accounts, CNY and multi-currency wallets, and are strongly viable for TikTok Shop mass payout, ad-spend funding and recurring supplier payments. Legal constraints: these EMIs are not licensed by the SBP, are not eligible depositaries, and cannot function as the exclusive treasury home; balances above the short-term operating float must be swept to an SBP-licensed bank. CRS and FATCA self-certifications and complete UBO disclosure are mandatory, partially eroding the PIF's private-beneficiary design but remaining acceptable when transparency is confined to regulated compliance channels.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance is the default at the tier-1 Panamanian institutions used for capital escrow and trade finance: the Foundation Council member or authorized signatory must attend an in-person identification interview before the SBP-regulated compliance officer; the founder and beneficiaries may act through the Panama Resident Agent. Remote onboarding by high-quality video liveness verification, document capture and apostilled submission is accepted by Banco General, Banistmo and Multibank once the counterparty is classified low-risk under the SBP's risk-based customer due-diligence rules; Towerbank and Banco Nacional, however, generally require a physical visit for escrow and capital accounts. Non-travelling directors may instead grant a notarized special power of attorney (Poder Especial) to the Resident Agent, executed before a Panamanian Notary or a Panamanian consulate, and have the agent complete the interview on behalf of the Foundation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Private Interest Foundation charter does not publicly identify the beneficiaries, colliding with bank-level UBO (ultimate beneficial owner) disclosure obligations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present to the bank's AML department: (i) certified English/Spanish copy of the Foundation Charter (Estatutos) naming the Founder, Council and Protector; (ii) current Public Registry standing certificate; (iii) Foundation Council Resolution appointing account signatories; (iv) sworn beneficial-owner declaration co-signed by the Panama Resident Agent, framed under Law 23 of 2015 and UAF record-keeping rules; and (v) a 'living letter of wishes' that identifies the beneficiary class for tax-reporting purposes while preserving legitimate commercial confidentiality.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume fragmented TikTok Shop consumer receipts (thousands of low-ticket transactions) may be misread as smurfing or transaction structuring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: File the official TikTok Seller Centre settlement pack: payout ledger, commission and SLS fee statements, seller verification certificate, live-commerce session identifiers, refunds and chargeback reports, monthly bridging P&L, and the bank account-opening questionnaire explicitly declaring the ISIC 4791 social-commerce model so that transaction-monitoring thresholds are set to the declared operating reality.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds for initial capital injection from related parties abroad (personal-account wires, CNY or other-currency remittances) triggers enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a notarized Source-of-Funds Declaration with 12 months of donor bank statements, prior TikTok Shop merchant-settlement documents if capital derives from earlier e-commerce earnings, gift or loan deeds, Foundation Council minutes approving the capital contribution, certified Spanish/English translations, and, where the founder is PRC-resident, the remitting bank's own compliance documentation evidencing lawful outbound transfer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Name-screening hits or negative-news results on beneficiaries and commercial counterparties (TikTok Pte. Ltd., Wise, Airwallex) imposing PEP or sanctions-based EDD.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver documented negative-news and PEP research using a recognized World-Check class database for all beneficial owners; confirm the platform and payment-partner licensing positions (TikTok Pte. Ltd. Singapore; e-money licences for Wise and Airwallex); provide a notarized statement that the PIF holds no bearer instruments, conducts no crypto-asset business, and operates an active retail commercial purpose consistent with its ISIC classification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: CRS/FATCA misclassification of the PIF as a passive investment vehicle rather than an active trade operator may trigger withdrawal of the banking relationship or 30-percent-type withholding leakage.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Secure tax-counsel opinion and bank-side categorization as an Active Non-Financial Entity (Active NFE) supported by the TikTok Shop operating contracts, actual seller-account history, reseller inventory and logistics agreements, payroll or contractor evidences, and the most recent financial statements demonstrating that active-business revenue substantially exceeds passive income; submit the appropriate W-8BEN-E and CRS self-certifications for controlling persons.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Protocol: (1) pre-notify the receiving SBP-licensed bank with the SWIFT BIC, beneficiary account, expected value date and amount; (2) instruct an MT103 in USD from the contributing party's bank with payment narrative reading 'APORTE DE CAPITAL A FUNDACIÓN DE INTERÉS PRIVADO LEY 25 DE 1995' plus the foundation's Public Registry identification; (3) lodge the Source-of-Funds questionnaire and the Council Resolution authorizing the account before value date; (4) if the capital is sourced from CNY merchant revenue, convert via Wise Business or the originating bank to USD and bridge through the local Panama clearing transfer, attaching the TikTok Shop payout stubs and supplier purchase orders; (5) retain the full nexus pack — TikTok Shop settlement files, sales invoices, purchase contracts, treasury authorization — for the bank and UAF paper trail. Neither the SBP nor the Ministry requires prior approval of inbound remittances; the true gate is bank-level KYC concluded during account opening.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing hierarchy: (i) SWIFT MT103 in USD for single supplier invoices above USD 15,000 with purchase-order and commercial-invoice references; (ii) documentary commercial letters of credit under UCP600, sight or 90-180 day usance, opened via Banistmo or Banco General and confirmed by Bank of China or ICBC for large consignment purchase orders; (iii) Wise Business or Airwallex mass-payout API for high-frequency TikTok Shop SLS fees, platform ad spend, refunds and small recurring supplier payments, riding on local ACH, FPS, SEPA, SWIFT and CIPS rails; and (iv) commercial Visa/Mastercard cards issued by Multibank or BAC for incidental platform charges. USD payments inside Panama clear on the local bank ledger because no central-bank RTGS exists; USD payments to the United States settle via each Panama bank's correspondent network (e.g., JPMorgan, BNP Paribas, BNY Mellon or Standard Chartered) through FedWire or CHIPS.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/CNH deliverable forward contracts (offshore CNH market, 1-week to 12-month tenors) under ISDA 2002 and CSA documentation executed through international dealer banks or SBP-licensed treasury desks, permissible without exchange-control authorization for a non-financial foundation.

USD/CNY non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) settled in USD against the offshore RMB or CFETS fixing, transacted through the licensed bank treasury or approved fintech FX counterparty in Hong Kong or Singapore, providing compliant hedging of CNY-denominated supplier exposures.

USD/CNH cross-currency swaps and FX options (including risk-reversal collars) for trade-liability management, requiring a Foundation Council treasury resolution, inclusion in CRS/FATCA asset declarations, and prudent structuring such that mark-to-market gains are sourced and managed outside Panama to preserve the territorial-tax exemption.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Flat Franchise Tax for Private Interest Foundation (Impuesto Anual de Personas Jurídicas)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Panama; payment processed through designated Registered Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by July 15; payment window generally January 1 through July 15 of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers a 10% surcharge plus monthly statutory interest; after three consecutive years of non-payment, DGI certifies the foundation as delinquent and the Registro Público de Panamá may administratively strike off the foundation, barring all commercial and statutory activity.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory independent audit for a standard offshore Private Interest Foundation; audit becomes compulsory only if the foundation conducts Panamanian-source taxable activities, becomes a regulated financial institution, or is required by its Foundation Charter, Council resolution, or banking/AML counterparties to engage a certified auditor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (NIIF) as adopted in Panama or Panamanian GAAP for any required financial statements; offshore non-taxable foundations may maintain books and records under IFRS, US GAAP, or other internationally recognized accounting standards.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Panamanian AML Law 23 of 2015, the Registered Agent must verify, maintain, and annually re-confirm current beneficial ownership records for each PIF; no standalone public UBO annual filing is required, but the foundation must immediately notify the Registered Agent of any change in beneficiaries or Foundation Council members, and such changes are recorded confidentially in the foundation's internal register.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficiaries and Protector (if appointed)
Minute Book of Foundation Council Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$1,500 - US$5,000 if an audit becomes necessary; otherwise no audit fee

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial regime: only Panama-source income is taxable; foreign-source income (including TikTok Shop sales to non-Panamanian consumers or goods domiciled abroad) is fully exempt. No reduced headline rate for retail; no special PIF tax holiday, but the foundation is structurally shell-neutral if all commercial activity occurs outside Panama.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 104 (Declaración de Renta Anual / Corporate Income Tax Return) filed electronically through the DGI's E-Tax 2.0 fiscal platform (Sistema Tributario Electrónico – Núcleo 2.0).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 3 months after fiscal year-end (calendar-year filers: March 31 of the following year). Quarterly advance payments (Anticipos) due April, June, September, and December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue. Under the territorial system, only Panama-source gross income from TikTok Shop live-commerce retail must be included.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PIF: segregate foreign-source TikTok sales (customers abroad, goods shipped ex-Panama) and either exclude them or report them only in the supplemental foreign-source income annex as exempt; do not intermingle.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Rentas Exentas o No Gravadas (Exempt/Non-Taxable Income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-exempt income items, including foreign-source gross receipts if properly documented.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach underlying evidence: logistic records, delivery addresses, TikTok payout statements, and payment-rail (Wise B2B) reconciliations proving the revenue was generated outside Panamanian territory.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Costos y Gastos Deducibles (Costs and Deductible Expenses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions attributable to Panama-source income, including COGS, creator commissions, logistics, storage, marketing, and administrative expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply direct/apportionment method to avoid double-counting expenses against exempt foreign income; maintain transfer-pricing correct allocations for creator/affiliate payments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Renta Neta Gravable (Net Taxable Income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Panama-source net taxable income after deductions and exemptions ($0 if all income is foreign-source).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute strictly within territorial scope; any reallocation of foreign profit to Panama by the DGI (e.g., management performed from Panama) must be avoided through factual substance evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for the four mandatory quarterly advance payments made during the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If no Panama-source taxable income, file a nil advance declaration (Form 531) each quarter with justification; late or unpaid advances attract surcharges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for Panamanian third-party withholdings (customers/clients) and mandatory attachments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach audited/local-prepared financial statements and Form 930 (Transfer Pricing Statement) if related-party transactions exceed the B/. 300,000 threshold.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% monthly surcharge on tax due, capped at 50%; late payment: 10% surcharge plus compounding default interest at DGI monthly rate. Failure to file Form 930: fine up to B/. 10,000 per year. Intentional non-filing with tax due above B/. 100,000 escalates to criminal tax fraud (2-5 years imprisonment plus fines of 1-3 times evaded tax).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% withholding on dividends distributed from Panama-source taxed profits; 0% withholding on distributions of foreign-source profits or capital (territorial system).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a DTA reduced rate (typically 5% for ≥25% shareholding, otherwise 10%/15%): (1) Recipient obtains an original or certified copy of the Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from its home tax authority; (2) Recipient presents a beneficial-ownership declaration to the Panamanian payer; (3) Payer files the DTA self-certification form with the DGI within the electronic withholding portal before making the distribution; (4) TRC and supporting declarations retained for 5 years to sustain the reduced withholding; (5) If TRC is unavailable, withhold at the statutory rate of 10% and obtain refund via DGI restitution process.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory WHT 12.5% (treaty-reduced to 10% under most DTAs; 0% if the IP is exploited entirely abroad under territorial sourcing). Interest: statutory WHT 12.5% (treaty-reduced to 10%; often 0% for interest paid to recognized foreign banks or to foreign lenders when proceeds are used outside Panama).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: B/. 300,000 (Panamanian Balboa equivalent to USD) in aggregate related-party transactions during a fiscal year triggers mandatory Form 930, Local File, and Master File documentation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regulations (Law 254 of 2021, Executive Decree 68 of 2022) apply if the PIF carries out 'relevant activities' (mortgage/housing, banking, insurance, IP, services, commerce, shipping). For the TikTok Shop retail scope, the relevant activity is 'commerce and shipping' of goods from Panama; the PIF/trader must maintain permanent physical premises in Panama, sufficient local employees, and actual direction of revenue-generating activities within Panama. Entities engaged exclusively in foreign-source passive income or foreign-commerce activities outside Panama fall outside ESR reporting, but the DGI retains power to recharacterize substance if management or logistics are actually conducted from Panamanian soil.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully misclassifying Panama-source TikTok Shop sales as foreign-source, omitting Payoneer/Wise/TikTok payout records, creating fictitious invoices, or deducting personal expenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI assessment with 40% deficiency surcharge (Art. 748 Tax Code), default interest at DGI monthly rate; criminal tax fraud (Arts. 280-A to 280-C Criminal Code): 2 to 5 years imprisonment and fines of 1 to 3 times the evaded tax; administrative closure of commercial registration; forfeiture of proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation Council members (directors) are jointly and severally liable for evaded tax and penalties if they signed or directed the false filing; courts issue airline 'prohibición de salida' (travel ban), freeze personal bank accounts, and extradite under bilateral/Interpol channels; civil liability extended to the founder if the foundation is proven to be a fraud vehicle.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Carrying out high-volume retail commerce through the PIF with no physical premises in Panama, no local staff, no board meetings in Panama, and no records evidencing management and operational control in Panama, while booking exempt foreign-source income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines of USD 10,000 to USD 1,000,000 for ESR non-compliance; DGI may request the Superintendency to cancel the Private Interest Foundation registration under Law 25 of 1995; automatic exchange of information with the protection's beneficiary country; loss of territorial exemption for related revenue due to source recharacterization.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the PIF risk individual sanctions, disqualification from directing Panamanian entities for up to 5 years, and personal liability for unpaid taxes and employer social-security contributions when the foundation is classified as a sham/alter ego.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the PIF as a front by receiving TikTok Shop funds into a personal wallet, paying suppliers through unregistered crypto/non-transparent rails, structuring daily payouts to avoid reporting thresholds, or conducting layering transactions with no commercial purpose.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalty for money laundering: 5 to 12 years imprisonment and fines up to B/. 10 million; asset forfeiture (extinción de dominio) of bank balances, inventory, and the PIF's assets; administrative penalties to the foundation's license under AML Law 23/2015.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The beneficial owner-founder and Foundation Council members are criminally liable as 'autoblanqueo' (self-money laundering); they face arraigo (travel restriction), preventive detention, bank account freezes, and automatic reporting to the Panamanian UAF (Financial Analysis Unit); international cooperation via GAFILAT and Interpol Red Notices.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file Form 930 with the annual return when related-party transactions exceed B/. 300,000; setting creator commissions, TikTok logistics fees, or management fees to a foreign affiliate outside arm's length; providing false comparability data.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Specific fine of up to B/. 10,000 for missing/inaccurate Form 930; DGI adjustment with a 40% surcharge on the deficiency plus default interest; if the adjustment indicates intentional undervaluation, criminal tax-fraud charges apply; public disclosure of the tax demo (flag) in DGI registries.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign inaccurate TP documentation face personal fines under Tax Code Art. 705-B; in fraudulent under-pricing, civil restitution of the artificially deflated profit is claimed personally from the directors; criminal prison term is elevated for coordinated acts across the PIF and affiliated seller entities.
